title: Delegation Evidence Orchestration for Short-Lived Credentials
author: Aisha Malik
content:
## Summary

This playbook defines the end-to-end evidence orchestration and forensics procedures for short-lived delegated credentials (temporary tokens, on-behalf-of sessions, and ephemeral service delegation). It is intended to ensure auditability, preserve required evidence for regulatory reviews, and enable rapid incident reconstruction while respecting data residency and retention obligations.

Audience: Security engineers, SREs, platform/identity engineers, compliance officers, incident commanders.

## Scope

- Systems covered: guardrail-authz (authorization gateway), edge-audit-collector, token-broker, evidence-archive, evidence-indexer.
- Credential types: bearer tokens issued by token-broker, STS-style delegation tokens, short-lived API keys (TTL <= 24 hours), and impersonation sessions.
- Regions: US, EU, APAC — residency mapping and retention rules are included below.

## Goals and SLAs

- Capture: 100% of delegation issuance and revocation events emitted to edge-audit-collector.
- Evidence visibility: all evidence indexed and queryable within 5 minutes (99th percentile).
- Incident assembly SLA: initial evidence bundle for triage delivered within 72 hours of incident ticket creation.
- Retention compliance: retention durations vary by residency (see table).

## Key definitions

- Delegation event: issuance, refresh, exchange, revocation, or prolongation of a short-lived credential.
- Evidence bundle: a time-bound package containing audit events, token metadata, service traces, access-control snapshots, and artifact checksums necessary for reconstruction.
- Temporal binding: cryptographic binding between issuance event and evidence snapshot (signed by evidence-archive signing key).

## Ownership and responsibilities

- Security: evidence policy, forensic playbooks, incident coordination.
- Identity/platform (owner: identity-team): token-broker changes, token schema, delegation lifecycle instrumentation.
- SRE/infra: edge-audit-collector reliability, evidence-archive availability, backup/replication.
- Compliance: retention policy signoff and audit packaging.

## Evidence signals and schema (required fields)

All delegation-related audit events MUST include the following top-level fields:

- event_id (string, UUID)
- event_type (string: delegation.issue | delegation.exchange | delegation.refresh | delegation.revoke)
- timestamp_utc (string, ISO8601)
- issuer_service (string)
- subject_type (string: user | service | workload)
- subject_id (string)
- delegated_scopes (array of strings)
- token_id (string)
- token_ttl_seconds (integer)
- purpose (string)
- request_context (string: path/query/headers fingerprint)
- residency_tag (string: US | EU | APAC | custom-region)
- auth_chain_signature (string: base64)

Example JSON event (shortened):

{
  "event_id": "d2f3a7b2-1e90-4a9d-9f7a-0b2d5e7c9f12",
  "event_type": "delegation.issue",
  "timestamp_utc": "2026-06-12T14:22:06Z",
  "issuer_service": "token-broker.prod",
  "subject_type": "service",
  "subject_id": "svc-data-transformer-01",
  "delegated_scopes": ["read:customer-data"],
  "token_id": "tk_0a9f...",
  "token_ttl_seconds": 3600,
  "purpose": "on-behalf-of ingestion job",
  "residency_tag": "EU",
  "auth_chain_signature": "MEUCIQDd..."
}

## Signal pipeline and reliability design

1) token-broker emits a delegation event synchronously to edge-audit-collector over gRPC with TLS and mTLS.
2) edge-audit-collector validates schema and assigns event_id if absent, then appends an ingestion receipt.
3) Events are sharded by residency_tag and token_id to ensure regional preservation.
4) downstream consumers: evidence-indexer (search), evidence-archive (cold storage), alerting-engine (policy violations).

Operational requirements:
- Acknowledgement timeout: token-broker waits up to 3s for collector ack; if timeout, it records issuance in local durable queue and retries with exponential backoff up to 1 hour.
- Event duplication tolerance: consumers must be idempotent based on event_id and token_id.

## Evidence packaging and temporal binding

When an incident is opened that involves delegated credentials, the following evidence bundle is required:

- ingestion-log slice (events +/- 24 hours around incident)
- token metadata snapshot (token_id -> issuance_time, ttl, scopes, issuer_chain)
- authz-policy snapshot (policy versions active at incident time)
- service traces and spans containing token_id or subject_id
- config and deployment snapshot for token-broker and guardrail-authz
- storage checksums for any affected artifacts (models, datasets)

Each bundle must be signed by evidence-archive using the temporal binding key, producing bundle_signature and signature_timestamp. The bundle metadata file must include a link to the signature and the evidence-indexer ID.

## Residency and retention mapping (table)

| Residency | Primary Storage | Minimum Retention | Export for Audit | Legal hold max |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| US | evidence-archive-us (encrypted, KMS: rwd-us-kms) | 3 years | Yes | 7 years |
| EU | evidence-archive-eu (encrypted, KMS: rwd-eu-kms) | 6 years | Yes (data subject redaction) | 10 years |
| APAC | evidence-archive-apac | 2 years | Conditional | 7 years |

Note: retention durations are minimums approved by Compliance. Exceptions require documented risk acceptance and must follow the control-exception process.

## SDLC integration (developer and release gates)

- Any change to token-broker, guardrail-authz, or edge-audit-collector must include:
  - Updated schema contract (JSON Schema) checked into evidence-schemas repo.
  - Integration test that produces representative delegation events and validates evidence ingestion end-to-end.
  - Security review (owner: security) for changes affecting auth_chain_signature or residency tagging.
  - Release gate: deployment blocked until evidence-indexer integration test passes in staging.

Checklist artifact sample (to attach to PR):
- schema-file: schemas/delegation.v2.json (sha256)
- e2e-test log: artifacts/delegation-e2e-2026-06-12.log
- staging-evidence-indexer-id: idx-57f3

## Incident response: delegated credential playbook (step-by-step)

1) Triage: classify incident type (unauthorized use | token theft | policy bypass) and record affected token_ids.
2) Immediate containment: call token-broker revoke(token_id) for all suspect tokens and verify revocation events surfaced to edge-audit-collector.
3) Preserve evidence: create a forensic snapshot job that packages ingestion-log slice and snapshots; sign bundle via evidence-archive.
4) Forensic analysis: authorized analysts may request decryption keys from KMS custodians (approval required: incident commander + legal).
3) Impact assessment: use evidence-indexer queries to enumerate resources touched by token_id.
4) Root cause: correlate auth_chain_signature, change-logs, and deployment snapshots to determine attack path.
5) Remediation: apply policy fixes (example: tighten scope, reduce TTL), rotate service credentials if lateral movement is detected.
6) Post-incident: assemble audit-ready evidence packet and forward to Compliance within 7 days.

CLI examples:

- Revoke token (token-broker):
  rwdctl token revoke --token-id tk_0a9f... --region eu

- Create forensic snapshot (SRE-run):
  rwdctl evidence snapshot --token-id tk_0a9f... --window 24h --sign --output /tmp/evidence-bundle-<id>.tar.gz

- Query evidence-indexer (Kusto-like):
  SELECT event_id, event_type, timestamp_utc, issuer_service FROM delegation_events WHERE token_id = 'tk_0a9f...' AND timestamp_utc between ago(24h) and now()

## Evidence consumption and audit packaging

- Compliance pack must include: evidence bundle, bundle_signature, chain-of-custody log (who accessed the bundle), decryption key release approvals, and residency declaration.
- Packaging format: tar.gz containing manifest.json, events.ndjson, policy-snapshots/, traces/, checksums.sha256 and signed by evidence-archive.

## Control exceptions and risk acceptance

If a development need conflicts with retention/residency (for example, cross-region debug trace export), apply the Exception Process:

1) Create a control-exception request in the Governance portal with: justification, data items, retention window, compensating controls.
2) Security + Legal review within 5 business days.
3) If approved, record exception_id in evidence bundle metadata and ensure additional monitoring is enabled.

## Monitoring and alerting rules (excerpts)

- Missing issuance events: alert if token-broker issues >100 tokens/min but edge-audit-collector ingests <95% of that rate over 10m.
- Large TTL deviations: alert if delegated token TTL > 24h in production.
- Residency mismatch: alert when residency_tag of event != region of issuing instance.

## Forensic hygiene and privacy controls

- Access to evidence bundles is logged and requires justification; access is timebound (default 7 days).
- Sensitive fields (PII) must be redacted in exported compliance packs unless Legal authorizes full export.

## Related pages and references

- /security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/entitlement-provenance-and-retention-framework-2026
- /security-and-compliance/audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025
- evidence-schemas repo: https://git.redwood.internal/evidence-schemas/tree/main

## Metrics to track

- delegation_event_ingest_latency_p99 (target < 5m)
- evidence_bundle_sign_time_p95 (target < 10m)
- evidence_bundle_assembly_sla_met (target 95% within 72h)

## Glossary and appendices

Appendix A: Token lifecycle diagram (text):
- Client -> token-broker (issue) -> token used against guardrail-authz -> guardrail-authz forwards token_id to backend service -> backend logs token_id and event to edge-audit-collector.

Appendix B: Quick FAQ
- Q: When should we shorten TTLs?
  A: Default production TTL for delegation is 1h. Shorten to 5m for high-risk scopes (write:billing).

- Q: Who can request evidence?
  A: Security, SRE, Compliance, Legal. Requests by others must be approved by Security + Compliance.
